_comment: Path A realignment, Phase 0 (P0.1). The Constitution as structured data, not prose -- see D:\WorkSpace\NPDev\NPDev_General__OutsideRepo\NPDEV_REALIGNMENT_PLAN\NPDEV_PATH_A_REALIGNMENT_PLAN.md. Each law's `enforcement` is enforced|declared|aspirational, checked mechanically by scripts/quality/check-constitution-coverage.py: a law can be aspirational, but it cannot claim `enforced` for free -- that requires a named `checker` (a repo-relative path, optionally with a pattern) that actually exists in the tree. The eight laws below are the Path A charter as stated in the source proposal (Analisis_Visions_And_Proposal_Realign.txt / PATH_A_REALIGNMENT_ANALYSIS_2026-09-10.md line 16): model as sole durable truth; runtime artifacts disposable; domain rules in model/kernel; capabilities as contracts; technology-neutral model; the Anti-Drift Law; layered complexity; understandable by domain experts and AI.

laws.law: The model is the sole durable source of truth. Generated code is a projection of it, never authored directly as the thing that carries meaning.
laws.note: P0.2 (2026-09-10): GeneratedProjectionGuard now runs after every GeneratorFacade emission and fails generation on a planted violation (GeneratorFacadeProjectionGuardWiredTest). Narrow scope by design -- it forbids direct adapter instantiation / adapterId branching in generated Java, not a full thin-projection audit of every emitted line.

laws.law: A generated FinalApp can be deleted and regenerated from its model without losing anything that matters -- only `data`, `logs` and `secrets` survive regeneration, and that three-directory list is the same in every seam that spares it.
laws.note: The disposability claim is only honest if the spared-directory list can't drift between Build-NpdevApp.ps1, Build-ClaudeApp.ps1 and FinalAppAssembler.PRESERVED_APP_DIRECTORIES -- that's the twin-pair rule this checker enforces.

laws.law: Domain rules -- invariants, access, lifecycle -- are declared in the model and enforced by the kernel/validator, not hand-written into generated application code.
laws.note: Largely true by construction (SemanticValidator + kernel enforce access/lifecycle/invariants from the model), but no single checker measures 'no domain rule leaked into hand code' holistically -- GeneratedProjectionGuard's scope is narrower (adapter selection only). Revisit once P2's semantic graph validation (P2.3) exists.

laws.law: A capability a pack or app depends on is declared as a contract (requires/provides), never assumed as a concrete implementation baked into the consumer.
laws.note: Composition refuses when a pack's `requires` is left unbound by the consuming app's `provides`, naming the pack and the unbound key.

laws.law: The model itself carries no technology identifier. Spring is the platform's current runtime binder, not NPDev's identity, and a second binder must be addable without changing the model schema.
laws.note: Currently false in the schema itself: config.runtime REQUIRES springProfile and gradleTask, with no `binder` field. Becomes checkable once P0.6 (open the binder seam) lands -- see scripts/policy/constitution.json's own P0.6 task in helpers/tasks.json.

laws.law: Generation is deterministic: two runs from the same model produce byte-identical output. Drift between runs is a bug, not an acceptable variance.
laws.note: Generates one sample twice and SHA-256s every emitted file under ArtifactNP/ + App/, failing on any differing path (declared exclusions: npdev-build-info.properties, generation-run.json). Run by run-generator-gate.ps1.

laws.law: Basic features stay simple by default; escape hatches exist for real needs but are honestly branded for what they are, not disguised as first-class 'trusted' shortcuts.
laws.note: The escape-hatch mechanism exists (TrustedSource/javaHook/trustLevel across 119 files, 21 generator main classes) but is branded 'Trusted', the opposite of honest labelling. Becomes checkable once P0.4 (invert Trusted -> Untrusted Extension) lands.

laws.law: The model and its diagnostics are legible to both domain experts and AI agents without either needing to read generated code to understand what an application does.
laws.note: The AI knowledge substrate (knowledge/cards/*.json, MCP search tools, validated by build_knowledge.py --validate-only in the AI knowledge gate) is real but partial -- it describes the platform, not yet 'why does this model element exist' from a semantic graph. That's P2.2-P2.4's acceptance slice.
